questions.q: Why can a standard Oracle Fusion Payables inquiry screen often NOT answer a question like "every unpaid supplier invoice over $10,000 that's more than 30 days old" in one click?
options: Because it mixes a dollar threshold, an age calculation, and a payment-status filter all at once — a combination no single built-in screen is built for
Because Oracle Fusion has no screens for viewing invoices at all
Because the number $10,000 cannot be typed into any Oracle field
Because inquiry screens only show suppliers, never invoices
questions.explain: The question combines three separate conditions at once, which is exactly the kind of ad-hoc combination SQL is built to answer directly.

questions.q: What is the best description of what a SQL SELECT statement does?
options: It changes existing rows in a table
It describes the result you want, and the database figures out how to produce it
It deletes rows that match a condition
It is a step-by-step program describing exactly how to search the disk
questions.explain: SQL is declarative — you describe the desired result (what), not the retrieval mechanics (how).

questions.q: Which single SQL statement does this course focus on almost exclusively?
options: DELETE
UPDATE
SELECT
INSERT
questions.explain: This course is about reading and investigating financial data, which is what SELECT is for. Statements that change data belong to data-loading work.

questions.q: Which later course in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path covers INSERT/UPDATE-style data-changing work (loading data into Fusion)?
options: Oracle Fusion General Ledger
Oracle Fusion Security
Accounting Fundamentals for Oracle Professionals
FBDI and ADFdi
questions.explain: FBDI and ADFdi, later in this path, covers loading and changing data in Oracle Fusion — distinct from this course's read-only investigation focus.

questions.q: In `SELECT invoice_num, invoice_amount FROM ap_invoices_all WHERE invoice_amount > 10000;`, what does the WHERE clause do?
options: It names the table being queried
It filters rows down to only those where the condition is true
It specifies which columns appear in the result
It sorts the final result set
questions.explain: WHERE is the filtering condition — only rows where invoice_amount is over 10,000 are returned.
